name: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
history: A king's daughter and a landgravine who, widowed at twenty, gave her wealth to build a hospital at Marburg and served the sick there herself. She died at twenty-four. Legend says bread she carried to the poor turned to roses when her husband asked to see it.
meditation: Give something today that costs you.
life: Elizabeth was born in 1207, a daughter of King Andrew II of Hungary, and at four was sent to the Wartburg castle to be raised with Louis of Thuringia, her future husband. They married when she was fourteen and loved each other deeply; they had three children. Influenced by the Franciscan friars newly come to Germany, she gave generously to the poor, and in a famine she opened the granaries while Louis was away. In 1227 Louis died of fever on his way to the Crusade. Elizabeth left the court, made provision for her children and took the habit of the Franciscan Third Order. With her dowry she built a hospital at Marburg in honour of Saint Francis and nursed the sick there with her own hands, under the strict direction of Conrad of Marburg. She died in 1231 and was canonised four years later.
prayerTo: Saint Elizabeth, you were a princess who chose to be a servant, and you found Christ in the sick and the hungry. Pray for all who care for the suffering, for widows and the bereaved, and for me, that I may hold loosely to what I own and give freely to those in need. Amen.
penance: Give away something you value but do not need, or volunteer an hour at a hospital, care home or soup kitchen.
